summary: isSensitiveProviderKey (internal/store/peloton.go) excludes the normalized key "jointokens" (from Peloton's "join_tokens" field) via a new providerKeyRedactionExclusions map, checked before the substring-match needle list. join_tokens is a short-lived identifier used to join a live class session in progress, not a credential, but its normalized form contains the "token" needle so it was redacted from every stored live-class-join response. Redaction otherwise remains store-write-only (no change to the live/MCP passthrough path) -- confirmed as an intentional scope decision with the user, not an oversight. Any future regen must keep this exclusion; if a genuinely new field later collides with a redaction needle the same way, add it to providerKeyRedactionExclusions rather than loosening the needle list itself.
reason: MINOR #8 from a live post-fix verification sweep. Asked the user directly (a security/correctness tradeoff, not a pure bug) whether join_tokens is actually sensitive and whether redaction should extend to the live path: user confirmed it is not sensitive (a short-lived session-join identifier, not reusable outside that session) and that store-only redaction should remain as-is otherwise.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck all green. New test TestRedactProviderPayload_PreservesJoinTokensButRedactsRealCredentials confirms join_tokens survives redaction while a genuinely sensitive sibling field (session_id) is still redacted, guarding against the exclusion being implemented too broadly.
